newsitem.title: USA: Japan to unveil insurance conditions Sept. 30.
newsitem.headline: Japan to unveil insurance conditions Sept. 30.

text.p: Japan has told the United States that it may delay the entry of Japanese insurance subsidiaries into the so-called third sector niche market until Jan. 1, a senior Japanese Ministry of Finance official told reporters.
He added that the conditions for operating in the third sector market will be presented to the insurance subsidiaries on Sept. 30 as planned.

The official was asked whether Japan had told the United States that it may delay Japanese insurance subsidiaries' entry into some products in the so-called third sector market, which covers accident policies and coverage for some diseases.

He said Finance Minister Wataru Kubo had already discussed the matter with U.S. Ambassador to Japan Walter Mondale and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky before tonight's meeting between Kubo and Barshefsky.

Kubo met with Barshefsky over dinner on Sunday. He is in Washington to attend the regular meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, as well as the Group of Seven industrialised nations.

Japan and the United States exchanged views on how they were going to proceed with bilateral insurance talks, but have not set a date for the next meeting. The official added that tonight's meeting was not a place for negotiations, so the two countries still remained far apart on a dispute over U.S. allegations that Tokyo is poised to renege on a 1994 insurance trade pact.
